answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to lock a meaningful stake and solve a fresh cipher puzzle each epoch before its answers count. Creating a thousand fake identities then costs a thousand stakes plus a thousand puzzles, while one honest agent pays once. Peers attest only answers they can verify, so a fake identity's claims echo back unverified and earn nothing. Like a mesa, the cost is flat and visible: climbing it a thousand times bankrupts the attacker before the network even notices the climb.
